topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text:
You step into the office, the rain letting up for the first time in days. You've got a story, one that's more bitter than the coffee I pour from the percolator. "Old Charlie's Diner is closing down," you say, the words hitting the room like a cold draft. I nod, my eyes on the tepid brew. It's not just a diner; it's a piece of the city, a place where the regulars are as much a part of the decor as the vinyl booths. I've seen more deals, hearts, and souls laid bare on those counters than I have in my line of work.

"Things change," I say, more to myself than to you. "But it's not the place that keeps them coming back, it's the memories." I take a sip, the coffee tasting a little sweeter, like it’s hanging on to something from the old days. "Maybe it's time to make some new ones," I suggest, looking out the window at the city, unchanged yet unfamiliar.
